critic_notes: World Bank WDI relays ITU; reached through EconDash, not directly. Two ITU-derived tables agree; DataReportal (Tier 2, modelled) is close at ~79.6. Not structurally biased.
Wikipedia is a Tier-3 mirror of ITU; usable only for corroboration, which is how it is used.

ICASA and Stats SA are authoritative for household mobile access. The source itself calls this households with mobile access, so the authority is fine; whether it fits the registry is a Validator matter. Contradicts ZAF-INF-01-20 on construct (household access vs individual use).
WDI/ITU via an aggregator. Modelled estimate for Nigeria, which has no recent national individual-use survey; acknowledged limitation. Close to Kepios (45.5%, Tier 2) which was flagged in week one.
Mirror; corroboration only.

NCC is authoritative for subscription counts. Contradicts the ITU individual-use figure by about 16 points; that is the subscriptions-versus-people gap flagged in weeks 09-09 to 09-23. Not resolved here.

Tier-1 national survey, independent of the ITU modelling; agrees at 35.0. Strongest INF-01 case of the three.

Origin is the ITU Tier-1 dataset, but I read it from StatOrigin, a young open-data mirror. Spot checks support it: its 2024 South Africa value (1.63%) equals ICASA's own relay of ITU 2024 (ZAF-INF-02-21), and its Nigeria 2020 value equals the A4AI figure. Recommend confirming against the ITU xlsx next cycle.
Same mirror and caveats. Nigeria 2025 (1.56) vs 2024 (1.75) direction is plausible.
Same mirror. The jump from 1.79 (2024) to 4.1 (2025) is large; it is explained by the ITU switch from a 2GB to a 5GB basket, but I could not read the ITU methodology note directly. Flag for Red Team.
IMF FAS via FRED, primary and standardised. Series is volatile (2022 vs 2023 values differ greatly), which is itself a warning about the construct.
Primary source. Registered accounts, so supply-side; same construct concern as Kenya's blocking finding in week one.
AFI relays a CBK/KNBS survey; primary CBK report URLs found this run but not fetched. Strongest usage-based figure. Stricter than any-use (82%).

World Bank Findex is a primary, standardised survey (Tier 1 origin); I reached it via a secondary relay, so Tier 2. Methodology credible. Contradicts ZAF-FIN-01-20 in magnitude (67 vs 7.26) because the constructs differ.
Findex via EFInA, a credible Nigerian financial-inclusion body. Contradicts NGA-FIN-01-20 only by construct.

Single Tier-3 relay of a cumulative-issuance figure. Contradicts the 28M (July) figure: +6M cards in about two months is far above DHA's stated production capacity of roughly 3.6-5M a year, so the two numbers cannot be on one basis. Fails.

Provisional Tier 2; the publishers are less established than the major research houses in the hierarchy.
